# Requirements Document

## Introduction

**Every existing diagram is rewritten to use the central diagram library.** This specification depends on `diagram-library` being implemented: that one builds the single canvas component, the declarative diagram definition and the event API, and proves them on two reference canvases; this one takes the remaining modules there and removes what the library makes redundant.

**Why this is its own specification rather than the library's last task.** The migration is the larger half of the work by file count — twelve modules, eighteen canvas files — and it is the half with the regression risk: the library can be built without touching a shipping canvas, but adoption rewrites every one of them. Separating the two means the library's approval is a judgement about a design, and this one's is a judgement about risk and sequencing. It also means adoption can land module by module behind a stable library, instead of the library shifting under the modules migrating onto it.

**What adoption means, precisely.** A migrated module supplies a diagram definition, a model mapping, and event handlers — and deletes its hand-built orchestration: private drag/pan/connect state, private anchor rendering, private connector paths, private toolbox-drop handling, private label editing. `drag-and-drop-centralization`'s survey counted the duplication this removes: eight private `dragRef`s, ten private `panRef`s, four private `connectRef`s, seven private `zoomBy`s, five private toolbox-drop handlers, six private anchor renderings. After full adoption those counts are zero, and that is checkable.

### The population, measured

Twelve implemented modules, eighteen canvas files: `ansible-structure` (1), `azure-pipeline` (1), `c4` (1), `causal-loop` (1), `databricks` (4 — three registered wrappers around one inner `DatabricksCanvas`, so one migration covers three readings), `dependency-graph` (1), `helm-charts` (1), `mindmap` (1), `rdf` (4), `sparql` (1), `timeline` (1), `wardley-map` (1). The two reference canvases `diagram-library` builds end to end are already migrated when this specification starts; the set to migrate here is **the remainder, measured at implementation time** — a fixed list written today would be stale by then, and this repository has produced six differing counts of one population in a single day by trusting written-down numbers.

## Alignment with Product Vision

The product's premise is that adding a diagram type means adding a module, not editing the shell — and after adoption that promise gets stronger: a new module is a definition and a mapping rather than a thousand-line canvas. The rewrite itself adds nothing a user can see; its value is that every diagram behaves identically where behaviour is shared, and that the next feature (a new gesture, a new route, multi-select) lands once instead of twelve times.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — Every module migrates, and the set is measured, not inherited

**User Story:** As the owner of this repository, I want every implemented diagram running on the library, so there is one canvas implementation to maintain, extend and trust.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN this specification is implemented THEN every implemented diagram module's registered canvases SHALL render through the library — the set measured at implementation time against `src/diagrams/*/client/register.ts`, with the measurement recorded.
2. WHEN databricks migrates THEN its three registered wrappers and the shared inner canvas SHALL migrate as one unit, and the three-readings-one-canvas structure SHALL be preserved, since it is a feature of that module rather than an accident.
3. IF a module cannot migrate — a visualization the library cannot express despite `diagram-library` Requirement 9 — THEN the gap SHALL be raised against the library and recorded, and the module SHALL be left on its hand-built canvas rather than half-migrated. **A module is on the library or it is not**; a canvas that renders through the library but keeps a private gesture path has the maintenance cost of both.

### Requirement 2 — Behaviour parity: the rewrite adds nothing and loses nothing

**User Story:** As a user, I want every diagram to look and behave after the rewrite as it did before, except where shared behaviour was already inconsistent — in which case I want the library's one behaviour.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a module migrates THEN every capability its canvas had SHALL survive: the same elements drawn, the same relations drawable, the same context actions, the same labels editable, the same keyboard behaviour. Deliberate unifications — a canvas whose pan or zoom deviated from the shared behaviour adopting the shared one — SHALL be recorded per module as they are made.
2. WHEN a module migrates THEN no new capability SHALL ride along. A migration that also adds a feature cannot be reviewed as a migration; anything the library newly makes possible for that diagram is follow-up work, recorded and left.
3. WHEN a module's migration lands THEN the `tests.md` entries exercising that diagram SHALL be re-run and their outcomes recorded with the build observed — these are the checks that catch what jsdom cannot, and a rewrite of the rendering path is exactly what they exist for.
4. WHERE `docs/screenshots/` images or the touch points named in `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md` are made misleading by a migration THEN the same change SHALL retake and update them, per the standing documentation rule.
5. WHEN a module migrates THEN its existing unit tests SHALL keep passing or be honestly replaced: a test of deleted private machinery is deleted with it, a test of behaviour is rewritten against the library seam and **seen to fail** against a deliberate behaviour break before it is trusted.

### Requirement 3 — The deletion is the deliverable

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the duplicated machinery gone, not shadowed — the point of a central library is what stops existing.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN adoption completes THEN the surveyed private machinery counts — drag state, pan state, connect state, zoom handling, toolbox-drop handling, anchor rendering per canvas — SHALL be re-measured and SHALL be zero across migrated modules, with the before/after measurement recorded.
2. WHEN adoption completes THEN the no-private guard family SHALL extend to the library's ground: private connector path construction, private shape rendering for library-expressible shapes, and private gesture state in a migrated module become offences the guards name — each guard carrying the established canary and mounting where it verifies behaviour.
3. WHERE a migrated module retains genuinely notation-specific rendering — a custom shape via the library's custom-shape contract, wardley's evolution axis — THEN that is not an offence, and the guard's exclusions SHALL name such cases with their reason rather than loosening the check.

### Requirement 4 — Sequencing: module by module, hardest evidence first

**User Story:** As the person approving risk, I want the migration ordered so that the riskiest assumptions are tested earliest, and each landing leaves the product releasable.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN modules migrate THEN each SHALL land independently through the four gates — the product is releasable after every merge, with migrated and unmigrated modules coexisting.
2. WHEN the order is chosen THEN the early migrations SHALL be the ones that test what the references did not: whichever of the axis-shaped (wardley-map, timeline) and the budgeted-graph (rdf) cases was not among `diagram-library`'s two references comes first here, because a library gap is cheapest the moment it is found and dearest after ten modules are on it.
3. WHEN this specification is worked THEN one Developer SHALL own it throughout, per the standing rule — the modules are independently landable for ordering and clean merges, not for extra hands.

### Requirement 5 — The shell and its registrations end the migration stronger

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the shell contract untouched and the known registration defect class closed by construction.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a module migrates THEN `client/register.ts` SHALL remain its seam with the shell — same `registrations` shape, same MIME matching — so the shell needs no change and notices nothing.
2. WHEN a module migrates THEN its canvases SHALL register view controls and toolbox **as the pair** the library provides by construction, closing the half-registration defect (canvases registering one and looking finished) for every migrated module; and the guard asserting the pair over mounted registered canvases SHALL lose that module from its exclusion list, never gain an entry.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Performance

- No migrated diagram SHALL feel worse than it did: drag latency, pan smoothness and open-to-first-paint are compared per module before and after on the largest example documents in `src/examples/`, and a regression is a blocker for that module's merge, not a note.

### Process

- Implementation follows the standing rules: one worktree per this specification, worktree identity set at creation, the four gates green on the merged tree before every land, and a fresh-tree build before trusting the first green.

## Out of Scope

- **The library itself** — any gap found here is raised against `diagram-library`, not patched in a module.
- **New features on any diagram**, including the follow-ups migrations reveal (wiring `fitToView` where a canvas never had one, new relation types the definition would now make cheap). They are recorded and left.
- **Backend and wire changes** — none, as with the library.
- **Removing the library's coexistence support** for hand-built canvases; that cleanup has its own moment, after the last module migrates.
